title: Tanzanian Mussels in Coconut
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Chaza wa Nazi — fresh Zanzibar mussels steamed open in a fragrant coconut milk broth with garlic, ginger, and lemon grass. Simple, fast, and extraordinarily good — the broth is as important as the mussels.
longDesc: Zanzibar mussels collected from the tidal rocks by coastal women — incredibly fresh, they need almost nothing beyond coconut milk, garlic, and heat. The steaming broth mopped up with chapati until the bowl is empty.
ingredients: 1 kg fresh mussels — scrubbed and debearded
steps: Discard any mussels already open that do not close when tapped.
Combine coconut milk, water, garlic, ginger, lemon grass, chilli, and turmeric. Bring to simmer.
Steam 4—5 minutes until all mussels opened.
Discard any that did not open.
Add lemon juice and coriander. Serve in the cooking broth.
chefTips: Discard unopened mussels before and after cooking.
Do not overcook — mussels toughen rapidly.
Provide chapati to mop up the broth.
cookingScience: Mussels open when heat denatures the adductor muscle protein holding shells closed. Continuing to cook after opening causes over-contraction of proteins — rubbery result.
sustainabilityTips: Mussels are filter feeders — they require no feeding inputs and clean the water around them. Among the most sustainable seafood available.
culturalNote: Mussels in coconut broth — shellfish collected an hour ago, cooked in coconut from the trees above the beach, eaten at the water's edge. Nothing more is needed.
